title: Depth Zero K Type
body_html:
Depth Zero K Type

For \(G=U(V)\), a depth zero \(K\)-type is a pair \[ (x,\rho) \] where \(x\) is a vertex in \(B(G)\) and \(\rho\) is an irreducible representation of the finite quotient \[ G_x/G_{x,0+}. \] For a covering group \(\widetilde G\), a depth zero \(K\)-type is similarly a pair \((x,\widetilde\rho)\), where \(\widetilde\rho\) is an irreducible genuine representation of \(\widetilde G_x/G_{x,0+}\).

Depth zero \(K\)-types are considered up to \(G\)-conjugacy. A depth zero supercuspidal datum \((x,0,1,\rho)\) gives such a \(K\)-type, and it is supercuspidal exactly when \(\rho\) is cuspidal for the finite reductive quotient.
